newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian election not delayed in flood-hit Manitoba.
newsitem.headline: Canadian election not delayed in flood-hit Manitoba.

text.p: Canada's chief electoral officer said on Sunday that a federal election for parliament called for June 2 will not be delayed in flood-ravaged Manitoba.
But Jean-Pierre Kingsley, the chief elections officer, said he would modify voting procedures for affected areas by moving polling stations and taking other steps.
Canadian Prime Minister Jean Chretien called the election a week ago, a decision that has drawn sharp criticism from many Manitoba residents and opposition politicians.

Under Canada's British-style system, the nationwide poll will elect members of parliament from every district and determine whether Chretien retains his post as prime minister. Chretien's Liberal Party holds a commanding lead in opinion polls.
Kingsley toured the disaster area and said he consulted with local officials before concluding it would still be feasible to hold the vote.
"I am confident Manitobans generally will be able to vote June 2 along with other Canadians," Kingsley told a news conference in Winnipeg.
However, he said the battle against the flood and the ensuing clean-up would mean that "there will be some people who will not be able to participate as fully as others."
